clocks.label: SALALAH TALKS
clocks.why: Gulf foreign ministers meet Iran's Abbas Araghchi in Oman on managing Hormuz shipping. This clock prices GEO-013 at 76 per cent - whether any arrangement preserves Iranian transit-administration machinery - and Tehran now arrives having watched a SECOND chokepoint close without lifting a finger.

clocks.label: FOMC DECISION
clocks.why: The meeting behind GEO-029, held at 72 for a third session rather than re-marked on an oil headline. Watch the statement's sentence about energy rather than the rate: the ECB dropped look-through last week, and whether the FOMC follows is the whole question.

clocks.label: BOJ DECISION
clocks.why: The second leg of the August-2024 yen-carry template GEO-025 is built on. A hike into a strong dollar is the mechanism that turns a funding trade into a forced unwind; Takata is on record that the Bank should move nimbly.

clocks.label: HORMUZ FALSIFIER
clocks.why: Our own deadline, not anyone else's. If the named escalation has not occurred by this date, non-occurrence is scored AGAINST this desk's escalation model rather than rolled forward - which is the entire difference between a forecast and a vibe.

clocks.label: XI IN WASHINGTON
clocks.why: The state visit behind GEO-006, raised to 92 today on the outside view. It also resolves the question the Delhi summit raised: whether Xi's call for BRICS peacemaking in the Gulf was positioning for this room, and what he asks for in return.

clocks.label: G20 MIAMI
clocks.why: Now a dated clock rather than a rumour, because GEO-005 moved on it. Zelenskyy has said yes; the scoreable object is whether the Kremlin confirms ATTENDANCE, which requires the host to have solved the legal problem of an ICC warrant first.

speculation.obs: The public trackers now disagree about how closed Hormuz actually is, and the gap is the intelligence. gCaptain reported seven vessel transits on Thursday against eleven the previous day and a ten-day average of ten, while IMF PortWatch logged six transits on 6 September against a pre-crisis baseline near 85 a day and TankerMap's AIS analytics page has been showing roughly 21 a day - and PortWatch publishes the reason for the divergence itself, since it counts AIS-broadcasting crossings only and hulls that stop transmitting are never captured.
speculation.read: Labelled inference: if the true flow sits between the counts, the difference is dark tonnage moving under a permit regime rather than trade that stopped. That would mean the strait is being rationed and monetised, not sealed - a toll with a guest list - and every 'Hormuz closed' figure sourced to AIS is a floor rather than a measurement.
speculation.falsifier: Discharge-side port-call data at Asian terminals would settle it. If arrivals match the low transit count at the usual lag, the collapse is real; if arrivals exceed it, the missing hulls are dark, not absent.

speculation.obs: The satellite fire-detection read on the Saudi pipeline is openly contradictory between specialists. NBC News reported imagery showing a 60-mile smoke plume along the route south of Medina with high-temperature readings at several infrastructure sites, and other reporting described fires detected simultaneously at six points; the Payne Institute's VIIRS Nightfire analysis of the same nights found emergency flaring at flares already catalogued and explicitly no new fires at uncatalogued locations. A Copernicus Sentinel image dated 10 September shows black smoke over the desert south-east of Medina along the general Petroline route, and Reuters noted there was still no independent confirmation the line itself was struck.
speculation.read: Labelled inference: those readings reconcile only one way - a long plume plus heat at KNOWN flare locations is the signature of a line being depressurised in a hurry along its length, not of six fresh holes in the steel. If that is right the damage is smaller than the imagery looks and the outage is a valve decision, recoverable in days rather than months.
speculation.falsifier: High-resolution imagery showing excavation or repair crews at named mileposts would prove rupture. A restart inside two weeks with October volumes unchanged would prove depressurisation.

speculation.obs: Shipping-intelligence analysts report that Bab el-Mandab traffic was running near normal until the week Perim fell, and that the tracked numbers understate it. Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 223 AIS-enabled transits between 10 and 16 August with at least 252 transits in a single late-August week, broadly in line with post-blockade levels, while noting that some tankers switch off AIS during loading and then exit via Suez - and Suez Canal traffic hit roughly 1,090 transits over four weeks, its highest since January 2024.
speculation.read: Labelled inference: if the strait was still carrying near-normal tracked volume three weeks before the island changed hands, then seizing Perim is a pricing event rather than a flow event - the Houthis took a gate traffic was still using, which is worth far more as a toll booth than as a barricade. It also means the war-risk premium, running around 0.5 per cent of hull value at Bab el-Mandab against 0.1 per cent in the Red Sea off western Saudi Arabia, is the number to watch rather than the transit count.
speculation.falsifier: Suez Canal Authority monthly transit and revenue figures, or a Lloyd's List weekly count showing Bab el-Mandab transits halving after the seizure, would settle whether this is a toll or a closure.

dossiers.name: Iran

glance.government: Islamic Republic - a clerical-military hybrid in which the security institutions have been ascendant since the February-May war
glance.leader: Mojtaba Khamenei, Supreme Leader since 8 Mar 2026, not verifiably seen in public for roughly six months; Masoud Pezeshkian president; IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi the operative center
glance.gdp: Roughly $300-390bn nominal depending on source; forecast to contract about 5% in 2026 with inflation near 70% and the rial at a record 2.02m to the dollar
glance.military: About 570,000-610,000 active (IISS puts it near 570,000) plus roughly 350,000 reserves; the IRGC Navy, not the regular navy, holds the strait
glance.influence: Transit rights and mine inventory at Hormuz, anti-ship missiles, Iraqi and Yemeni networks - set against oil revenue the central bank governor himself describes as having fallen to zero

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint, not the man. Iran is a state whose one convertible asset - the barrel - has stopped moving, which is why its remaining leverage is geographic rather than economic, and why it is spent in advertised doses rather than banked. The desk that decides is the IRGC Navy and the new wartime security committee, not the presidency and not the invisible Leader: Washington routed its own peace offer through career Guard commanders, and Iran's president has said on state television that communicating with Khamenei is very difficult. That produces exactly the behaviour this board keeps recording - a volley at forewarned bases in Jordan that was almost entirely intercepted, mines laid and lanes conditionally cleared, six near-breakthroughs that each end in a restated condition. Prospect theory says a cornered regime gambles, but a regime whose survival runs through an institution that profits from the crisis has an interest in holding the temperature where it can still choose it. The falsifier is a strike that actually kills Americans, or a verified minesweeping calendar with published coordinates - either would show the temperature is no longer being chosen.

concerns: Mine and anti-ship capability at Hormuz is intact and reversible - a cleared lane is a maintenance schedule, not a settlement
Succession is unresolved in practice: an unseen Leader plus an IRGC that answers Washington's messages is a leadership fiction with a real chain of command underneath
Oil revenue near zero against 70% inflation removes the economic off-ramp that would normally price restraint
Escalation is now probabilistic rather than intentional - interception rates, not decisions, separate a message from a casualty event

Retaliation has gone HORIZONTAL: fire into US facilities in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait in a single night widens the number of surfaces on which the interception equilibrium can fail, and converts Gulf hosts from venues into potential parties

The war has reached the LOADING POINT: Iranian state media says four US missiles hit a tanker six miles off Kharg on 5 September, and Iran fired anti-ship and ballistic missiles toward the strait the day before. Unconfirmed, and the terminals themselves are still unstruck - but the one asset with any convertible value left is now inside the target set

A SECOND CHOKEPOINT, bought without an Iranian casualty: with Ansar Allah holding the Yemeni bank of Bab el-Mandeb, Tehran now has a hand on two of the six places where seaborne trade passes single file. Note what that does to the bargaining table rather than the battlefield - a Red Sea chip is SEPARABLE, tradeable away without Iran conceding anything of its own, which makes a Hormuz settlement cheaper for Tehran and not more expensive. The principal-agent risk runs the other way: Ansar Allah has its own war aims at Taiz and its own scores with Riyadh, and a proxy that acquires territory acquires independence

dossiers.name: Saudi Arabia

glance.government: Absolute monarchy; day-to-day rule exercised by Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman on behalf of King Salman
glance.leader: Mohammed bin Salman, Crown Prince and PM; the decisive desks are the Royal Court, the Ministry of Defence under Khalid bin Salman, and Aramco
glance.gdp: Roughly $1.1tn nominal; fiscal breakeven oil price is materially above the pre-war Brent strip, which is why a high barrel is not simply good news for Riyadh
glance.military: About 250,000 active across services plus the SANG; heavily equipped and air-dominant, with a demonstrated shortage of deployable INFANTRY - the constraint that just cost it Mocha
glance.influence: Spare crude capacity, Ras Tanura and Yanbu as the world's principal loading complex, and since the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement a publicly stated Pakistani security commitment

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint. Riyadh's problem is not resolve, it is force structure: it can generate air strikes in a day and cannot generate a brigade that will hold a coastline, which is why its Yemeni position is a patchwork of rival Saudi- and Emirati-funded militias that has now lost Mocha, Dhubab and the island of Perim in a single week. Today the second constraint became visible and it is the more consequential one. The kingdom's eastern outlet has been shut by the Hormuz permit regime since the war; its western outlet runs past a strait whose eastern bank is now held by Ansar Allah; and the Ministry of Energy has now CONFIRMED that the East-West pipeline feeding Yanbu - the one export path that avoids Hormuz altogether - was shut as a precaution after drone strikes launched from Maysan province in Iraq, though Aramco itself remains silent and no force majeure has been declared. On OPEC's own numbers August production fell to its lowest since 1990. The desk that decides is the Royal Court plus Aramco, not the foreign ministry, and Aramco's revealed preference across fifty years is to protect its reliability franchise: after Abqaiq in 2019 it lost about half its output and still declined to declare force majeure, delivering from storage. The third fact of the day is the one that changes the strategic picture rather than the barrel: Mohammed bin Salman asked the American president twice on Thursday for strikes on the Houthis and was refused, receiving intelligence, targeting data and a CENTCOM visit instead. Sagan's security model prices what follows - a client hedges when the credibility of its guarantee falls, not when the threat rises - and the hedging instruments to watch are reactor tenders, enrichment language and further operationalising of the Mecca pact with Pakistan, not a bomb. The falsifier remains a strike on an EXPORT terminal rather than a refinery: that is the rung at which Riyadh stops taxing its own margins and starts losing its only convertible asset.

concerns: Both westward outlets are CLOSED at once - Perim and the eastern bank of Bab el-Mandeb are held by Ansar Allah, Petroline is confirmed shut, and Hormuz remains under permit; the post-2019 redundancy architecture is gone
No deployable ground force in Yemen - coalition units withdrew from Mocha and from Perim rather than hold them, and air power cannot retake a coast
The American guarantee has been publicly tested and found partial: freedom of navigation for the lane, intelligence and targeting data for the land war, no strikes
Refining capacity is being taxed repeatedly: Jazan, 400,000 b/d and about a tenth of Aramco's net refining, has been hit or shut three times since late July, and Tuesday's assault injured at least 73
Export infrastructure at Ras Tanura and Yanbu remains untouched - still the single most consequential unfired tripwire on this board
Fiscal breakeven above the strip means a war premium does not pay for itself; the kingdom needs volume as much as price, and volume is what both a terminal strike and a pipeline outage would take

dossiers.name: Russia

glance.government: Presidential autocracy with a managed legislature; State Duma elections due September 2026
glance.leader: Vladimir Putin - the only decider on the war file; Peskov is a thermostat, not an actor
glance.population: About 144 million (2026 estimate; occupied-territory counting disputed)
glance.gdp: Roughly $2.7tn nominal; the government cut its 2026 growth forecast toward 0.4-1%, with oil and gas revenue reported down more than 25%
glance.military: About 1.3 million active with roughly 2 million reserves; defence spending near 6.3-6.5% of GDP
glance.influence: Sanctioned-barrel logistics including the Arctic route, Africa Corps guarantees in the Sahel, energy leverage over Europe, veto and nuclear status

dossiers.summary: Moscow's constraint is refining and money, not morale. Ukrainian deep strikes have pushed refinery runs to about 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since 2002, and the fuel export ban first imposed in July is being weighed for a second extension - each extension a public admission of how much capacity is offline. The deciding desks are the defence and finance ministries rather than the foreign ministry: the September Duma election and the 6.3-6.5% of GDP the war costs are what price the negotiating posture, which is why the deep pause Peskov announced reads as a bargaining position taken from a front that is still moving at Pokrovsk. Watch where the state chose to spend a scarce asset this weekend - Africa Corps, roughly 200-300 personnel supplied overland through Burkina Faso, was used to save a junta in Niamey, buying an advertisement and incurring an obligation in the same act. The observables that would move this file are not statements but airlift and diesel: Flight Unit 224 traffic above its six-flight run rate, or refinery runs recovering past 4m barrels a day.

concerns: The fuel and refining constraint is the real bind - denial is working where punishment has not, and Kyiv is aiming at exactly that
The announced campaign against Ukraine's grid is punishment by Pape's definition, with a poor historical conversion into concessions
Sahel guarantees now carry a defend-the-palace obligation a 200-300 person detachment cannot scale
September Duma elections and a possible post-election reserve call-up are the domestic clock every diplomatic signal is priced against

The covert front against the supplier coalition is now formally attributed: Berlin blames Moscow for an explosive drone at Leipzig/Halle and closes the Bonn consulate on Sept 18, with the EU calling it state-sponsored terrorism - salami tactics against logistics rather than against forces

First reciprocated pause of the war, and it is a bargaining instrument rather than fatigue: Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for 72 hours from midnight on 5 September, explicitly tied to the American envoys' visit, hours after striking Ukrainian airports and infrastructure and with Ryabkov restating that Washington must accept realities on the ground

dossiers.name: Ukraine

glance.government: Wartime presidential republic under martial law; national elections suspended for the duration
glance.leader: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, constrained by coalition dependence; Rustem Umerov holds both the negotiating brief and the intelligence file
glance.population: About 39.5 million on mid-2026 estimates - wartime displacement makes every figure soft
glance.gdp: Roughly $225bn nominal (2025); the EU agreed a package of about EUR 90bn for 2026-27, funded by market borrowing rather than by seizing the roughly EUR 210bn of frozen Russian assets
glance.military: About 677,000 active on the IISS count; larger figures circulate and are not verified
glance.influence: A deep-strike drone campaign that has taken Russian refining to a 24-year low, the Black Sea corridor, and the political weight of being the coalition's test case

dossiers.summary: Kyiv's constraint is arithmetic - manpower, interceptors and a donor calendar - and it sets the strategy rather than following from it. The one instrument Ukraine owns outright is the drone campaign against Russian refineries, which is denial in Pape's sense and is measurably working; nearly everything else is rented from capitals that vote. That dependence is why the deciding desk is now split between the general staff and a negotiating channel run through Washington, and why Zelenskyy has to say yes to the joint Western plan and no to surrender in the same breath. It also explains Myla: an army under sustained deep strike disperses munitions into settlements, which lowers the odds of losing a depot and raises the odds of a night like Friday's, when 38 people died mostly from what the warehouse contained. The falsifiable claim for the winter is that Russia's fuel constraint shapes Russian behaviour more than blackouts shape Ukrainian negotiating positions - if Kyiv's position visibly softens under grid attack while Moscow's does not under fuel shortage, the model is wrong and we say so.

concerns: The announced Russian campaign against the electricity grid arrives with winter and with air-defence stocks already rationed
Pokrovsk is the axis Moscow names when it explains why it is in no hurry to talk; its fall would be a step change, not a line move
Funding is market-borrowed rather than asset-backed, which puts the money on a European political calendar
Dispersal of munitions into inhabited areas makes mass-casualty events recurrent regardless of anyone's aimpoint

dossiers.name: China

glance.government: Party-state under the most centralized leadership since Mao; a recent command purge reshaped the military timetable
glance.leader: Xi Jinping; Wang Yi carries the foreign file with delegated authority
glance.gdp: About $20.9tn nominal (IMF, 2026); 4.7% growth in the first half against a 4.5-5% target, July exports up 23.9% year on year
glance.military: About 2.0 million active, the largest standing force in the world; announced defence budget in the $280bn range
glance.influence: Buyer of last resort for sanctioned barrels, rare earths and the export machine, coast-guard jurisdiction pressure around Taiwan and the East China Sea, and a summit Washington wants

dossiers.summary: Beijing's constraint this quarter is the calendar, not the doctrine. A state visit on 24 September and a tariff truce expiring in November are both worth more than any concession on Iranian crude, which is why the buying continues while the rhetoric stays defiant - and why Treasury sanctioned an Egyptian bank's UAE branches rather than a Chinese one. An enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive. The desk to watch is not the foreign ministry but the coast guard and the customs administration: PLA sorties around Taiwan have been declining while jurisdictional assertion has been rising, and that ratchet - salami tactics in Schelling's sense, slices too thin to fight over individually - is the actual instrument. Read the summit as accumulation under cover of detente rather than as a thaw, and keep the discount small: announced head-of-state visits with active staff preparation happen about 90% of the time. The tell that breaks the benign read is a coast-guard action inside the visit window; the tell that breaks the leverage read is a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before 24 September.

concerns: Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building around Taiwan, not the event itself
China is the load-bearing leak in the Iran sanctions siege - Mulder's rule is that a siege is only as tight as its leakage path
The tariff truce expires in November, just after the summit, which is where a cheap concession becomes an expensive one
A defiant public line paired with quiet compliance makes intent unreadable from statements; only flows settle it

dossiers.name: Israel

glance.government: Parliamentary democracy; the Knesset dissolved in July and the election is set for 27 October 2026
glance.leader: Benjamin Netanyahu, prime minister; Israel Katz defence minister and the cabinet's designated hawk
glance.gdp: About $720bn nominal on 2026 estimates, with defence spending near 8% of GDP
glance.influence: Air superiority over the Levant, the Washington relationship, and an undeclared nuclear status the state has never confirmed

dossiers.summary: Read every Israeli decision for the next seven weeks through 27 October. That is the constraint, and it is a calendar rather than a character: a prime minister facing an election needs deliverables that are visible, mapped and finished, which is exactly what a declared security zone is. On 4 September Katz said the capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge completes the phase of securing control in southern Lebanon and that there will be no withdrawal until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout the country - a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to meet, which makes the presence open-ended by construction. The desk that decides is not the cabinet podium but Northern Command's force-generation math and the finance ministry's reserve-duty bill, because holding ground costs manpower in a way air power does not. Note also the direction this cuts: history says a held buffer produces chronic attrition rather than episodic campaigns, which is why this board CUT its multi-week-campaign odds on the day the zone was declared. Separately, national security minister Ben Gvir published a twenty-page plan for what he calls voluntary emigration of Gaza's population - 250,000 in the first year and the remainder over six more. It is a minister's document rather than cabinet policy, and forced transfer of civilians from occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions; it is logged here as a coalition signal, not as a programme.

concerns: The 27 October election makes restraint politically expensive at exactly the wrong moment
A withdrawal condition the Lebanese state cannot satisfy converts an operation into an occupation by definition
The Lebanon framework still has no third-party verifier and the party being disarmed rejects the premise
Ministerial transfer plans for Gaza, even unimplemented, carry legal and coalition exposure that outlasts the cabinet

dossiers.name: Germany

glance.government: Federal parliamentary republic; sixteen Laender, each electing its own Minister-President. Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote 20 September 2026
glance.leader: Friedrich Merz, chancellor, whose CDU just lost 25 of its 40 seats in Saxony-Anhalt; Ulrich Siegmund leads the AfD there and has said he will not stand for Minister-President without a stable majority
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.9tn nominal - unverified against a current print; Jaguar Land Rover cutting 4,000 jobs and Volkswagen repurposing a plant for defence are the texture of the industrial quarter
glance.military: About 182,000 active on standard counts, with rearmament running against recruitment shortfalls; unverified against a current IISS figure
glance.influence: Europe's largest industrial gas consumer, the logistics bridge to Ukraine through Leipzig/Halle, and the swing vote on every EU sanctions and energy instrument

dossiers.summary: Germany's constraint stopped being abstract on Sunday. The AfD took 43.9 per cent and 39 of 83 seats in Saxony-Anhalt on turnout that rose from about 60 to about 80 per cent, and the CDU fell to 17.2 per cent - which means the late-mobilisation argument that has contained the AfD in every previous Land election did not work, and ING said so in as many words. The desk that now decides is not the federal party presidium in Berlin, which can only expel people; it is the Landtag running ballots in Magdeburg, where a third round for Minister-President is settled by a simple majority of votes cast and the five-seat BSW can decide the outcome by abstaining. Underneath the politics the older vice is unchanged: Germany replaced Russian pipeline gas with seaborne LNG, trading a political dependency for a maritime one, so a war at Hormuz reaches German industry directly - and it remains the physical bridge over which munitions reach Ukraine, which is why a drone came down at Leipzig/Halle rather than at a barracks. Two more elections land on 20 September.

concerns: A Land where no majority exists without breaking one of two taboos - the CDU has excluded both the AfD and Die Linke, and the third-ballot rule rewards deadlock
Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote on 20 September, thirteen days after the mobilisation defence visibly failed
Fraud narratives spread within hours of the count, part of them traced by DW's fact-check desk to the Matryoshka influence operation - contested results are now a standing feature of German elections
A sabotage campaign aimed at logistics rather than forces sits deliberately below any alliance threshold, and Lavrov has answered Berlin's attribution by calling it the start of a real war
Energy input cost remains the binding industrial number, and seaborne LNG means Hormuz is now a German domestic-politics variable

dossiers.name: United States

glance.government: Federal presidential republic; midterm elections 3 November 2026
glance.leader: Donald Trump; Scott Bessent at Treasury, Marco Rubio at State, Pete Hegseth at Defense, Kevin Warsh at the Federal Reserve
glance.gdp: Roughly $30tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; federal debt past $40tn
glance.military: About 1.34 million active with roughly 770,000 reserve and National Guard; budget in the $900bn range
glance.influence: Dollar clearing and OFAC designations, CENTCOM escort of the strait, and a rate path that prices everyone else's oil bill

dossiers.summary: The American constraint hardened today and it is arithmetic rather than politics. August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, which removes the soft-landing argument for cutting; simultaneously diesel set an all-time record at $5.820 a gallon on a refining shortage no interest rate can fix. That is the RESCUE WITHHELD configuration - a market pricing help in a shock where help does not exist - and the long end already agrees, with the ten-year at 4.79% and the thirty-year at 5.27%, both above this board's published red lines, and the reverse-repo buffer down to $0.70bn. The desk that decides is not the podium: it is the FOMC, the refiners' turnaround calendar and the weekly EIA distillate print, in that order of who can actually change the number. Foreign policy is being run on the same logic - allies invoiced for contributions at Hormuz, a Venezuelan venture organised around one man's legal exposure rather than around built infrastructure, and a president who declined this week to say whether the United States would defend Britain in another Falklands war. Each of those is leverage bought cheaply now against a commitment payable later.

concerns: Record diesel is the invisible half of the inflation problem, because it prices freight, farming and heating rather than only the pump
A hot labour print into a hiking debate removes the monetary rescue markets keep assuming
Enforcement at Hormuz is now a standing commitment - a lane you must keep clearing is not a victory
Alliance ambiguity is being used as leverage in three theatres at once, and credibility spent in one is not recoverable in another
Confirmed American casualties would collapse the intercepted-volley equilibrium the whole restraint posture rests on

dossiers.name: Japan

glance.government: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system; Bank of Japan policy decision due 18 September 2026
glance.leader: Emperor Naruhito as head of state; the offices that matter for this file are the Bank of Japan policy board and the Ministry of Finance FX desk - not the cabinet
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.2tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; policy rate 0.75 per cent, a thirty-year high, with ten-year government bond yields near 3 per cent for the first time since 1996
glance.military: Self-Defense Forces of about 247,000 active personnel; defence spending on a path toward 2 per cent of GDP
glance.influence: The world's cheap funding currency, one of the largest foreign holders of US Treasuries, and a carry trade estimated anywhere between $500bn and over $4tn depending on definition

dossiers.summary: Japan's constraint became visible in a number this week: 15.4 trillion yen, about $98.6bn, spent in a single month defending the currency, and reporting that it likely sold US Treasuries to fund it. For thirty years Japan supplied the world with money that cost nothing and the world spent it on everything from Mexican bonds to American technology; that arrangement is unwinding because Japan finally has inflation, imported partly through a weak yen and partly through an energy bill that this year's Hormuz disruption made worse. The desk that decides is the BoJ policy board on 18 September, and the yen has already run to 154.06 on the expectation. What is genuinely new is the American side of the plumbing: Washington joined the July intervention and Bessent pushed the Fed to widen the FIMA repo facility, which lets Tokyo borrow dollars against its Treasuries instead of selling them. Read that as the balance-of-financial-terror being actively managed - the US needs its largest foreign creditor not to become a seller during a heavy issuance calendar, and it built a valve to make sure.

concerns: A disorderly carry unwind transmits a Tokyo rate decision into global asset prices within hours, as it did in August 2024
The size of the borrowed-yen stack is genuinely unknown - published estimates span an order of magnitude
A currency defence funded by Treasury sales raises US long-end yields at the exact moment the ten-year sits above 4.75 per cent
A defence financed by repo must be repeatedly refinanced, which converts a one-off intervention into a standing obligation
Imported energy costs are the transmission line from the Strait of Hormuz into Japanese inflation and therefore into this policy decision

scenarios.q: What if the Houthis turn Perim into a toll booth?
scenarios.read: They already own the paperwork. The Houthi-run Humanitarian Operations Coordination Center has published a voluntary, free 'Safe Transit Request' scheme since 2025 - 48 hours' notice, ship name and passage details, an answer within a day - and in August the movement explicitly denied any plan to charge, citing the UNCLOS rule against levying fees for mere passage. Holding Perim is what converts that paperwork into an office. The Sound Dues logic says a chokepoint holder prices access rather than denying it; the counter-pressure is that Egypt's Suez revenue and the movement's own legitimacy project both argue for keeping it free and voluntary, which is currently worth more to them than money.

stages.s: A. Safe Transit Request volume rises and the HOCC publicises compliance as recognition
B. Notification becomes de facto mandatory - a named non-compliant vessel is attacked or turned back
C. A published requirement, or a charge for a named 'service' - escort, pilotage, inspection
D. War-risk quotations stop distinguishing Saudi-linked tonnage from general trade

scenarios.falsifier: A Lloyd's or Joint War Committee note showing the Saudi-linked carve-out intact through October, with Bab al-Mandab transits within 10 per cent of August's tracked count, kills stages B through D outright.

scenarios.q: What if Petroline restarts inside two weeks?
scenarios.read: The Payne Institute's VIIRS nightfire analysis found emergency flaring at flare sites already in its catalogue and explicitly no new fires at uncatalogued locations, which is the signature of a line being depressurised fast along its length rather than holed in six places. If that reading is right, the outage is a valve decision and the repair is short. What does not recover on the same timetable is the exit: a restarted pipe still delivers to Yanbu, and Yanbu still ships past Perim, so the bullish case for crude survives the bearish case for the pipeline.

stages.s: A. Ministry or Aramco announces a restart, no force majeure declared
B. October Yanbu loading programme published at normal volumes
C. Brent gives back the week's roughly 9 per cent gain
D. Insurers narrow the Bab al-Mandab premium back toward general Red Sea levels

scenarios.falsifier: High-resolution imagery showing excavation or repair crews at named mileposts would prove rupture and kill stage A; the nomination window passing in silence would do the same.

scenarios.q: What if Putin accepts the Miami G20?
scenarios.read: Acceptance would be the first two-sided signal since the talks froze, and it would be an ATTENDANCE decision rather than a peace decision - a head of state under an ICC warrant landing on American soil requires the host to have solved a legal problem in advance, which is itself part of what is being negotiated. Lawrence Freedman's point holds: what Putin wants is political recognition no armistice text can grant, so a meeting opens a bargaining round rather than closing a war. The Lyman reversal cuts both ways, because a side losing ground has more reason to talk and less reason to concede.

stages.s: A. Kremlin confirms Putin will attend the summit
B. A leader-level bilateral is formally scheduled
C. A published framework text with a dated ceasefire start
D. A ceasefire actually holding more than 30 days

scenarios.falsifier: Peskov restating the 'deep pause, no new proposals' line after a formal invitation is issued kills stage A, and with it everything downstream.

chatter.claim: That the CIA's release of the pre-9/11 presidential briefs is the official admission of foreknowledge - that 'they knew' is now documented in the government's own paper, and that putting it out on the 25th anniversary is a limited hangout designed to absorb the question rather than answer it.
chatter.spread: The dominant reading across a dozen simultaneous /pol/ anniversary threads and widely amplified on X.
chatter.read: This is the frame with a real kernel, which is why it travels: the briefs do show sustained strategic warning about hijackings, dirty bombs and aircraft used as weapons. The move the claim makes is to collapse strategic warning into tactical warning - knowing an attack is wanted is not knowing the flights, the date or the cell, and the whole intelligence-failure literature lives in that gap.

chatter.claim: That World Trade Center 7 could not have collapsed the way the official account says, with the argument now anchored on Barry Jennings - the building's deputy director of emergency services, who described hearing explosions inside before the towers fell - and on the claim that molten steel was still running at Ground Zero weeks later, which no office fire could produce.
chatter.spread: Two dedicated high-reply /pol/ threads plus video reposts, running all day on the anniversary.
chatter.read: The oldest structural claim in the file, revived every year and boosted this year by the declassification. It does not survive the NIST collapse reports, and the molten-metal observation has mundane candidates including underground fires burning for weeks in a debris pile. Reported here because belief in it is the data point, not because the mechanics hold.

chatter.claim: That Howard Lutnick survived 9/11 because he took his child to school for the first time ever that morning, offered as a 'they were told' data point rather than as coincidence.
chatter.spread: A high-reply /pol/ thread, recycled every anniversary and boosted this year by his public profile.
chatter.read: Textbook survivorship reasoning. In a city of eight million on a weekday morning, thousands of people missed those buildings by an ordinary accident of routine, and only the ones who later became famous get a thread. The claim is unfalsifiable by construction, which is exactly why it never dies.

chatter.claim: That a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles episode showing the Technodrome crashing through New York aired on a broadcast channel on the 25th anniversary as deliberate signalling, part of a wider 'predictive programming' catalogue of pre-2001 media said to depict the attacks.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ happening thread with listings screenshots, plus a dedicated predictive-programming thread on /x/.
chatter.read: Coincidence-mining against a syndicated cartoon run that airs three times a day with a fixed rotation. The frame is durable because the search space is effectively infinite - decades of media, any image of a damaged skyline counts - so a hit is guaranteed and is then treated as a signal.

chatter.claim: An ethnic-scapegoat narrative is circulating heavily around the 9/11 anniversary, in competing versions that each substitute a named religious or national group for the mechanism of the attack.
chatter.spread: Very loud on /pol/ in several directions simultaneously, and reported this week as spreading through large podcasts and anniversary-driven archive footage on X and Instagram.
chatter.read: Reported as a phenomenon, not repeated as content. The persuasion technique is consistent across every version: replace an institutional question - who failed, which desk, which warning went unactioned - with an identity question, which cannot be checked and therefore cannot be lost. The tell is that the circulating versions are mutually exclusive and structurally identical.

chatter.claim: That the 'drones from Iraq' attribution on the Saudi pipeline is a manufactured pretext, and that the real author of the strike is being concealed in order to license a move against Baghdad.
chatter.spread: Several /pol/ threads and the running Persia-Israel general.
chatter.read: Standard casus-belli-manufacture framing applied to an attribution that was genuinely single-sourced at first. The kernel that cuts against it: Baghdad's own investigation confirmed the launches came from Iraqi soil and it sacked its Maysan commander over them, which is a costly admission no government volunteers to serve another state's pretext.

chatter.claim: That Saudi exports have dropped to zero and that 70 per cent of the kingdom's oil is now shut off from world markets.
chatter.spread: Two all-caps /pol/ happening threads and viral repost screenshots.
chatter.read: Checkably wrong in a specific way. Petroline is a bypass line of roughly 5 million barrels a day of capacity against Saudi output near 6 million, and the kingdom's principal Gulf-side terminal at Ras Tanura is not on it. The real number is bad enough without inflation - August output fell 2.3 million barrels a day to about 6 million, the lowest in more than thirty years.

chatter.claim: That Saudi Arabia is finished as a state - 'a fake state created after the fall of the Ottoman empire, only propped up by the US, kept content with oil money, beaten by Iran, beaten by the Houthis, pipeline blown up, straits blocked'.
chatter.spread: A high-reply /pol/ thread, and the framing is spreading well beyond it this week.
chatter.read: The collapse-of-the-Gulf-monarchy frame, which recurs at every regional shock and has a poor record. The checkable part is real and serious: two export routes impaired at once, output at a thirty-year low, and a crown prince reported to have called Washington twice in one day for military help. State failure and a very bad quarter look identical from outside and are not the same thing.

chatter.claim: That Putin has expelled the Rothschild family from Russia entirely and that they are now forbidden from setting foot on Russian territory under any circumstances.
chatter.spread: A high-reply /pol/ thread built on an amg-news aggregator post.
chatter.read: A recurring fabrication from a site that generates financial-cabal stories on a schedule. The structural tell is that no decree number, no ministry and no legal instrument is ever cited - only the assertion that one exists.

chatter.claim: That the Ukraine war is theatre, with Europe continuing to buy Russian gas offered as the proof - 'Russia is going to kill us, and we will keep paying them so they can'.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread citing a Euronews report, alongside the permanent Ukraine generals which now give flatly contradictory accounts of the same front near Lyman.
chatter.read: The 'both sides are the same management' frame. The kernel is real and documented - European energy payments to Russia continued long past the sanctions rhetoric - but that is a policy failure under price and industrial pressure, which is a different object from a staged war.

chatter.claim: That the air traffic control meltdown which cancelled around 2,000 UK flights was caused by a military aircraft deliberately feeding spurious flight data into the system, with the circulating versions naming a foreign air force rather than accepting an equipment fault.
chatter.spread: Circulating on X and picked up on the boards after reporting that a military aircraft was being blamed for the outage.
chatter.read: Downstream of a real and unusual fact - reporting does attribute the outage to a military aircraft's data - which is exactly the shape a rumour needs in order to travel. The leap is from 'a military aircraft caused it' to 'a specific state did it on purpose', and the document that settles it is the NATS incident report, not a thread.

chatter.claim: That Congo's Ebola outbreak is not a natural event - versions include that it was commissioned by the Congolese presidency as a political fabrication, that aid organisations imported it to unlock funding, that a simple cure is being withheld, and that the virus is an engineered bioweapon.
chatter.spread: Heaviest in French-language TikTok video and in rumour networks inside the affected provinces, circulating since May and documented in mainstream reporting on the outbreak.
chatter.read: The standard health-disinformation playbook, and the artificial-origin variant follows a template run against HIV, Ebola and COVID for decades. The kernel worth taking seriously is the consequence: documented vaccine refusal in Ituri and Kivu slows ring vaccination, so the rumour is an input to the case curve rather than commentary on it.

easy.bottomLine: Saudi Arabia had two ways to get its oil out without going past Iran. In about thirty hours it lost both. A big pipeline across the desert was knocked out by drones that flew from Iraq, and rebels in Yemen took over the land and the island next to the narrow sea gate the oil uses on the other side. Saudi Arabia asked America to bomb the rebels. America said no, twice, and offered maps and information instead.
easy.risk: Still high, for the seventeenth day in a row. It only goes to the top level if an American is killed or an American ship is hit in the fighting going on now, and that has not happened for ten days. The new worry is not a battle - it is that a country asked its big protector for help and did not get it.
easy.markets: Oil is above 100 dollars a barrel and finished the week about nine per cent higher, but it actually dipped on Friday, the day the rebels took the island. That is because the world's energy watchdog said people will use a lot LESS oil this year, since it has become too expensive - the biggest drop since the pandemic. Diesel at American pumps is a record 6 dollars 6 cents a gallon, up from 3 dollars 71 a year ago.
brief: Saudi Arabia's big oil pipeline was shut down after drones flew from Iraq and hit it, and at almost the same time Yemeni rebels took the port and island next to the narrow sea gate the oil has to pass through. Those were the only two ways Saudi oil could avoid going past Iran, and now both are blocked.

The BRICS group of countries, which includes China, Russia, India and Brazil, met in New Delhi and all agreed on one statement. They talked about wanting peace and their own way of paying each other instead of using dollars, but again they did not actually set one up, which is what would really matter.

Ukraine quietly spent four months attacking a bulge in the Russian lines near a town called Lyman, and has now cut it off and taken back more than 200 square kilometres. That bulge was the launch pad Russia had built over about a year and a half for attacking further into eastern Ukraine.

Ukraine's president said 'yes, of course' when asked if he would meet Putin at a big meeting of world leaders in Miami in December. Putin has not said yes, so this is one side wanting a meeting, not a meeting being arranged.

Talks between Israel and Lebanon that were supposed to happen in Rome this month have been pushed to October, and made smaller - just ambassadors meeting in Washington. Lebanon's president said there will be no new talks while Israeli attacks in the south keep going.
