risk.line: HIGH, held for a SEVENTEENTH consecutive pass, and what changed today is not a front line - it is a redundancy. Since the spring, every Gulf barrel that wanted to avoid Iranian inspection took one of two roads: the East-West pipeline across the peninsula to Yanbu, or the Red Sea exit at Bab al-Mandab. Both were taken off the board inside about thirty hours - the pipeline shut by drones launched from Maysan province in Iraq, the strait's mouth taken when Houthi forces seized Mocha, Dhubab and Perim island. The day's real signal is the answer, not the attack: Mohammed bin Salman asked Washington twice for strikes on the Houthis and was refused twice, receiving intelligence, targeting data and a CENTCOM visit instead. CRIT still requires an American killed or an American hull hit in the fighting now under way, and neither has happened in ten days.

forecasts.q: The Houthis or an entity they control publicly institute a MANDATORY transit requirement or any charge for Bab al-Mandab passage - a published rule, not a threat, not the existing voluntary scheme
forecasts.note: OPENED at 38, and the number is deliberately BELOW the tempting analogy. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing that licenses a design read at all: the Houthi-run Humanitarian Operations Coordination Center has published a voluntary, free 'Safe Transit Request' scheme since 2025 - 48 hours notice, ship name and passage details, an answer inside a day, non-sanctioned vessels only - and on 1 August the movement explicitly DENIED any plan to charge ships, citing the UNCLOS rule that bars levying fees for mere passage. Taking Mocha, Dhubab and Perim converts that paperwork into an office. The Sound Dues logic and Iran's own PGSA, stood up within about ten weeks of gaining strait leverage, both argue yes. It is held under 50 because the counter-incentives are specific and strong: the voluntary-and-free version already buys de facto sovereignty recognition at zero diplomatic cost, which is the movement's actual product; a fee would unite Cairo, whose Suez revenue depends on the same water, with the Gulf, and would invite the naval response Washington has so far declined to mount. If it comes, it will be priced as a SERVICE - escort, pilotage, inspection - not as a toll.

forecasts.q: Russian average monthly territorial gains in Q4 2026 fall below their Q2-Q3 2026 average (ISW/DeepState)
forecasts.note: 63, up five, and this is the biggest mover on the board. Michael Kofman's falsifiable claim - that Russian recruitment would stop covering casualties and offensive TEMPO would decline before any line broke - has until now been argued from casualty arithmetic. Today it has territory: Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps cut the Russian salient between the Nitrius and Zherebets rivers north of Lyman and retook more than 200 square kilometres, eliminating the springboard Russia spent roughly eighteen months building toward Sloviansk and Izium. The detail that makes it credible is the sourcing order - Russian military bloggers reported the reversal before Kyiv confirmed it, and they had no incentive to invent it. Capped at plus five for two reasons: ISW states plainly that public evidence is insufficient to size the counterattacks, and the Pokrovsk axis is untouched. The seasonal base rate independently supports the direction - autumn rasputitsa and winter have historically depressed mechanised tempo against summer.

forecasts.q: Saudi Arabia publicly announces enrichment, weapons pursuit, or a nuclear-sharing arrangement
forecasts.note: 21, up three, on the cleanest print this model has had. Glenn Snyder's alliance security dilemma says a junior partner reads what its patron REFUSES, not what it promises; Scott Sagan's security model attaches the consequence - states build when the credibility of someone else's guarantee falls, not when the threat rises. Today both halves printed at once. The threat leg: both Saudi westward outlets closed inside thirty hours, with Petroline shut and Perim in Houthi hands. The guarantee leg: the crown prince asked the American president twice for strikes and was refused twice, receiving intelligence, targeting data, roughly 160 to 200 personnel and an Admiral Cooper visit instead. This stays at 21 rather than 35 because the question asks for an OVERT announcement and hedging is normally covert - the number is a deliberate floor on a trend it cannot fully see, and the observables are a fuel-cycle clause, a reactor tender or Pakistani personnel, not a speech.

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, formal and holding more than 30 days
forecasts.note: 20, up two, and the smallness is the discipline. Three legs moved together for the first time since the talks froze: Zelenskyy told Deutsche Welle 'yes, of course' when asked whether he would meet Putin at the G20 the United States hosts at Trump National Doral on 14-15 December; American negotiators have shuttled between Kyiv and Moscow; and a Russian delegation confirmed attendance at the G20 energy meeting. It is only two points because willingness is the cheapest signal in diplomacy and it came from the side that wants the meeting - Putin has not reciprocated. The base rate governs the ceiling: 79 per cent of interstate wars end within two years, and this one is in its fifth, which is the part of the distribution where hazard rates DECLINE rather than rise. Long wars get longer. The falsifier is armed: Peskov restating the 'deep pause, no new proposals' line after a formal invitation kills the move.

forecasts.q: Major US and/or Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes (multi-day, state targets)
forecasts.note: 46, down two, and the cut is deliberately partial because this morning already spent two points on the same class of evidence and marking an echo is the error this desk has been caught making. The new facts are not echoes. Trump publicly attributed the pipeline attack to Iran - 'probably behind it' - and in the same set of remarks said the Houthis had asked the United States not to intervene, after refusing Riyadh twice. Revealed preference beats attribution every time: a president who will not strike the AGENT over a struck ally's pipeline is not about to reopen a multi-day campaign against state targets in the PRINCIPAL. An attribution the attributor will not act on is a declaratory move, not a predicate. The watch item that would reverse this is a Treasury designation naming the Iraqi group and its financial network - that is when words become an instrument.

forecasts.q: Front-month Brent settles at or above $120/bbl on any daily settle before 31 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: 49, down three, because the demand leg finally printed and it cuts against the barrier. The IEA's September report cuts 2026 world oil demand by 2.5 million barrels a day - 940,000 steeper than its August number and the largest annual contraction since the pandemic - with the losses concentrated in middle distillates and petrochemical feedstocks, and the rate of decline easing from 5.3 million in the second quarter to 2 million by the fourth. Supply falls further, by 5.7 million, with the Gulf recovery pushed to 2027, which is why this is a three-point cut rather than a rout. But the tape is the tell: Brent slipped below $105 on Friday, on the day Perim fell, up about nine per cent on the week and not squeezing. Stage discipline applies - a supply shock that meets demand destruction fizzles at Stage B, and the collapse ending is not the default ending.

33, up two: the political track slipped while the kinetic one did not. The US-mediated round scheduled for Rome this month has been pushed to October and downgraded to an ambassadors meeting at the State Department, and President Aoun said in Nabatieh there will be no new negotiations while Israeli operations continue. On the ground at least twenty-nine people have been killed in two weeks, Israel detonated a reported 1,100 tonnes of explosives inside the Ali al-Taher ridge on 11 September, and shelling hit al-Mansouri, Douha, Arnoun and Wadi al-Salouqi. Schelling's test caps the move at plus two: an operation that CONSOLIDATES a declared line is coercive bargaining, one that extends past it is a campaign, and both governments are still using the consolidation framing. Diplomacy receding is not the same thing as a campaign starting.

forecasts.q: Xi state visit to the US occurs in September 2026 roughly as planned
forecasts.note: 92, up two, and it is a routine outside-view raise rather than news. The visit is confirmed for 24 September at the White House, twelve days out, with no cancellation signal; Xi is travelling normally, and used the Delhi BRICS summit to call for the bloc to take a peacemaking role in the Gulf - which reads as pre-summit positioning, a leader arriving in Washington with something to sell, not a leader preparing to cancel. Announced head-of-state visits with active sherpa preparation are consummated more than ninety per cent of the time, and the residual shrinks as the date closes. This is the kind of move that should be boring; a forecast that only ever changes on drama is badly calibrated.

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover to more than 50 per cent of pre-war volume (about 65 a day against a 130 baseline)
forecasts.note: HELD at 10 for a NINTH instance of the same pattern. Gulf foreign ministers meet Iran's Abbas Araghchi at Salalah on Monday, the fourth dated venue this desk has watched produce an announcement rather than a transit. What has changed is Tehran's hand rather than its intention: a party that has just watched a second chokepoint close without lifting a finger arrives at a safety meeting with more to trade and less reason to hurry. Watch the meeting for a named administrator, a fee schedule or an escort arrangement - a toll regime always announces itself as a safety mechanism.

forecasts.q: The US ULSD diesel crack spread settles below $45/bbl on any daily settle before 15 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: HELD at 23 with the two new facts pointing opposite ways, which is the honest reason not to mark it. Against: Petroline's terminus at Yanbu also charges the Yasref and Yanbu refineries, roughly 650,000 barrels a day of distillate-heavy Europe-facing capacity, and a crude line that is not pumping cannot feed them. For: the IEA now expects the demand losses to fall most heavily on middle distillates, which is demand destruction in the exact barrel this question prices. Diesel at the American pump is a record $6.06 a gallon against $3.71 a year ago. When the supply and demand legs of a spread move the same way, the spread does not have to.

forecasts.q: The FOMC raises the fed funds target range at or before the 9-10 December 2026 meeting
forecasts.note: HELD at 72 for a third consecutive session, and the hold is a refusal to double-count rather than an absence of news. The energy shock got worse today and the board went RED for a fourth business day, but this question turns on a sentence rather than a barrel: whether the 16 September statement drops look-through on energy, as the ECB did last week. Marking an oil headline into a rate question before the committee has spoken is exactly the error the 6 September audit caught in this question's own history.

forecasts.q: USD/JPY appreciates 8 per cent or more from its 3 September level (160.0 to 147.2 or below) in any rolling 30-day window, before 31 Mar 2027
forecasts.note: HELD at 31 with a clean data vintage for a third session. The BOJ meets on 18 September and Takata is on record that the Bank should move nimbly - a hike into a strong dollar is the mechanism that turns a funding trade into a forced unwind, which is the whole reason this question exists. Nothing in today's energy shock touches the barrier arithmetic, and marking a yen question on an oil headline is the kind of cross-contamination this book is supposed to refuse.

forecasts.q: Saudi authorities publicly confirm a force majeure at Yanbu, Jizan or Ras Tanura, OR a reduction in East-West (Petroline) throughput, before 31 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: RESOLVED YES on 12 September - Brier 0.314, the worst score on this ledger against GEO-009's 0.029, mean 0.171 across two resolutions. Kept on the board rather than retired because the post-mortem is the point: the defect was in question DESIGN, not in the world. Joining two limbs with OR meant the easy limb - any throughput reduction - carried the question, and the Ministry of Energy's precautionary shutdown announcement satisfied it within a day of opening. A question that can be resolved by a press release is not a forecast.

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: Saudi Arabia loses both of its routes around the Strait of Hormuz
brief.h: Drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province forced the shutdown of the East-West pipeline on Friday, hours after Houthi forces completed the seizure of Mocha, Dhubab and Perim island at the mouth of Bab al-Mandab, closing the two roads Gulf crude had been using to avoid Iranian inspection.
brief.t: The important thing here is not that a pipeline stopped pumping. It is that the redundancy architecture the kingdom built after the 2019 Abqaiq strikes, precisely so that no single attack could ever reach the export tap, was neutralised in about thirty hours by a drone flight and an infantry advance down a coast road. Petroline exists to carry four to five million barrels a day across the peninsula to Yanbu so they never have to pass Iran; Bab al-Mandab is how those Yanbu barrels leave the Red Sea. Take out the pipe and you are back inside Hormuz under someone else's permit office. Take the strait's mouth and repairing the pipe only buys you a jetty that opens onto a gate you do not hold. Follow the money to the answer rather than the attack: Mohammed bin Salman asked the American president twice for strikes on the Houthis and was refused twice, receiving intelligence, targeting data and roughly 160 to 200 personnel instead - a security guarantee denominated in data rather than in ordnance, which is why our ledger raised the odds of a Saudi nuclear announcement rather than of an American one.

consp.claim: That the Houthi advance is not really Houthi - that Moscow quietly handed Yemen a capability it did not have, with a post attributed to Alexander Dugin, 'Russia may have given something special to Yemen', circulating as the tell; a separate thread insists Saudi oil exports have already 'dropped to zero' and the number is being suppressed.
consp.spread: The Dugin line ran on 4chan's /pol/ through 12 September alongside a high-traffic 'SAUDI OIL EXPORTS DROPPED TO 0' thread at well over a hundred replies, and the same framing circulates on X as speculation that Russian targeting data sat behind the Maysan drone launch.
consp.read: It maps onto the patron-capability frame, the same one applied to Iranian drones in Ukraine, and it has a checkable kernel: reporting in 2024 that Moscow weighed transferring P-800 anti-ship missiles to the Houthis, and Russia's own statement on 1 September that air defence is the main axis of military-technical cooperation with Iran. What is not checkable is the leap from a considered transfer to this week's events, which were an infantry manoeuvre against a collapsing militia patchwork, not a technological surprise. The export claim is measurably wrong rather than merely unproven - Saudi crude is still loading, and the Ministry of Energy's own statement describes a precautionary pipeline shutdown, not a halt to exports.

angles.effect: Naming Iran as 'probably behind it' keeps the pressure campaign's frame intact while justifying a NON-response; blaming the principal is far cheaper than striking the agent
Pays the bill either way - it dismissed its own Maysan operations commander and closed the Shalamcheh crossing with Iran to avoid becoming the target set
Gains a named culprit but not a defender, and an attribution it cannot act on converts directly into pressure for a deterrent of its own
Denies involvement and keeps deniability intact, because the launch point and the militia are Iraqi even where the supply chain is not

dec.kill: A US Treasury designation naming the specific Iraqi group and its financial network, or forensic recovery of the airframes showing Iranian production, would move this from 'probably' to evidenced.

brief.context: EPOCH first: this is a late chapter of the 1973-74 rail, in which American security guarantees were traded for dollar-priced oil and Gulf surpluses were recycled into Treasuries. The bargain's unstated term was that Washington would physically defend the flow, and the desk that decides whether it still does is not the podium - it is CENTCOM and the National Security Council, which this week supplied targeting data and declined ordnance. The permit the headline grants is to Ansar Allah: holding Perim converts a voluntary shipping-notification scheme into a plausible jurisdiction over the strait. The mechanism to name is Glenn Snyder's alliance security dilemma - a junior partner fears abandonment and entrapment at once, and reads what its patron refuses rather than what it promises - with Scott Sagan's security model attaching the consequence, that proliferation follows guarantee credibility rather than threat level. BASE RATE: overt nuclear announcements are rare because hedging is normally covert, which is why our ledger sits at 21 per cent and is explicitly a floor. INFLUENCE MAP: principal Tehran, agent the Iraqi militias and Ansar Allah, narrator the White House attribution, operator the valve at Yanbu and the guns on Perim, market the Bab al-Mandab war-risk premium, target Riyadh's export volume. FALSIFIER: an Aramco October loading programme for Yanbu published at normal volumes turns all of this back into a routing interruption, and a Joint War Committee note showing the Saudi-linked carve-out intact through October would say the strait is being priced rather than closed.

brief.head: BRICS adopts Delhi declaration as Xi urges the bloc to broker Gulf peace
brief.h: The 18th summit passed the New Delhi Declaration unanimously on Friday with Xi Jinping in India for the first time in seven years and Putin in the room, after Indian diplomats reconciled directly opposed Iranian and Emirati positions on the Gulf war to keep a single text alive.
brief.t: Read a BRICS communique for an INSTRUMENT rather than an aspiration, and this one again delivers the aspiration. Every summit since 2009 has promised an alternative to dollar settlement, and almost none has produced a named operator, a dated launch or a settlement volume - the reason is structural rather than rhetorical, because the bloc's surplus members want to be paid in something, and the only thing all of them will still accept from each other is dollars. What is genuinely new is the seating chart. Iran and the UAE now sit inside the same tent arguing about a strait one of them administers and the other one ships through, which makes the Gulf war an intra-bloc dispute rather than a West-versus-the-rest one, and explains why the declaration took drafting rescue to survive. That is also the frame for Xi's call for BRICS peacemaking twelve days before he lands at the White House: a leader who can say he is de-escalating the Gulf arrives in Washington with something to sell.

consp.claim: That a gold-linked BRICS settlement unit is being prepared for announcement and that discussion of it is being actively suppressed - 4chan's precious-metals general ran a 'Why the fuck was our thread nuked' edition on 12 September at roughly 270 replies, reading the deletion itself as evidence.
consp.spread: /biz/ precious-metals and 'Bitcoin vs gold for the next ten years' threads, plus recurring posts arguing the market is 'delulu' and oil is running out; on X the same expectation attaches to every BRICS summit week.
consp.read: This is suppression-as-confirmation, where an absence of evidence is converted into evidence of an effort to hide it, and it is unfalsifiable by construction - which is the tell rather than the refutation. The checkable kernel is real: gold volatility sits near 28.5 and central-bank buying has run above trend for three years, so the physical-versus-paper tension being gestured at exists. What does not exist is the instrument. Our ledger prices a Chinese third physical-metals venue at 20 per cent, and the honest test is a named operator with a dated launch, not a deleted thread.

brief.context: EPOCH: this sits on the 1944-73 rail, in which the settlement unit itself became a political object once gold detached, and on the 2022 rail of weaponised settlement, in which frozen reserves taught every surplus state that Treasuries are political instruments. The desk that decides is not the summit - it is each member's central bank and its exporters' invoicing preference, and Allison's Model III applies: where you sit is where you stand, so an Indian refiner buying discounted Russian crude in dirhams is the actual policy, whatever the communique says. MECHANISM: a reserve currency is a network good, and networks do not switch on announcements, they switch when the cost of staying exceeds the cost of leaving. BASE RATE: seventeen prior BRICS summits have produced expansion, development-bank capital and payment pilots, and zero functioning cross-bloc settlement units - the outside view says the modal outcome of summit eighteen is summit nineteen. FALSIFIER, which is what would make this a real story: a named operator, a launch date and a published settlement volume, or a member state invoicing a major energy contract in a non-dollar unit and disclosing the size.

brief.head: Ukraine cuts off the Russian salient north of Lyman
brief.h: Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps has eliminated the wedge between the Nitrius and Zherebets rivers that Russia spent roughly eighteen months building as its springboard toward Sloviansk, retaking more than 200 square kilometres in an operation kept quiet since May.
brief.t: What matters is not the square kilometres, it is which square kilometres. That salient was the base for the northern approach to Sloviansk and Izium and it sat astride the supply road into northern Donbas; removing it does not win a war, but it deletes an axis, and deleting an axis is how a defender buys a season. This is also the first territorial evidence for a named, dated claim rather than for a mood: Michael Kofman has argued for a year that Russian recruitment would eventually stop covering casualties and that offensive TEMPO would decay before any line broke, and until today that argument lived entirely in casualty arithmetic. The detail that makes it credible is the order of reporting - Russian military bloggers described the reversal before Kyiv confirmed it, and they had no incentive to invent it. ISW is careful and so are we: it says publicly available evidence is not yet enough to size the counterattacks, which is why this moves a probability five points rather than rewriting the front.

consp.claim: That the scale of Ukrainian success is manufactured for the cameras - a claim built on a quote attributed to Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev that Ukrainian drones carry extra tanks of mazut, heavy fuel oil, specifically to produce bright flames and smoke for the footage, framed as psychological operation rather than damage.
consp.spread: Running on 4chan's /pol/ inside the pro-Russian 'comfy happening' generals on 12 September and echoed in Russian Telegram commentary, while the mirror-image thread on the same board insists the Russian line has collapsed outright and a year of gains is gone.
consp.read: Two opposite claims about the same week on the same board is itself the finding: both sides' online formations are now optimised to score the FOOTAGE rather than the front. The kernel is checkable in principle, since incendiary payloads on strike drones are real and added fuel does increase visible flame, but it does not touch Lyman, which is a ground manoeuvre. The strongest reason to believe the substance is the sourcing order - the milbloggers reported the loss first, and a claim that costs its own side is worth more than one that flatters it.

brief.context: EPOCH: positional attrition war in the Donbas, whose ancestor rail is the 1916-18 Western Front problem - a defender with drones and mines now holds the advantage that machine guns and wire once gave, and the attacker pays in vehicles and infantry for metres. The desk that decides is the Russian General Staff's force-generation branch, not the Kremlin podium: tempo is a function of trained infantry and armoured stock, and both are consumed faster than they are replaced. MECHANISM: a salient is expensive to hold because it is fired on from three sides, so eliminating one converts an offensive asset into a defensive liability. BASE RATE: autumn rasputitsa and winter have depressed mechanised tempo against summer in every year of this war, which is why our Q4 question was already above even money before today. INFLUENCE MAP: principal the General Staff, agent the formations at Lyman, narrator the milbloggers who broke it, operator the drone and artillery units, market Western munitions supply, target the Sloviansk approach. FALSIFIER: ISW or DeepState mapping that fails to confirm the 200-square-kilometre figure, or a Russian recapture of the Zherebets line within six weeks, would reverse the five points.

brief.head: Zelenskyy says he would meet Putin at the Miami G20
brief.h: Asked by Deutsche Welle whether he would sit down with Putin at the summit Washington hosts at Trump National Doral on 14-15 December, Zelenskyy answered 'yes, of course', as American negotiators shuttle between Kyiv and Moscow and a Russian delegation confirms it will attend the G20 energy meeting.
brief.t: Willingness is the cheapest signal in diplomacy, and here it is being offered by the side that wants the meeting, which is why it moves our ledger two points rather than twenty. The structure worth watching is the venue rather than the handshake. A G20 the United States chairs, on American soil, hands Washington the lever mediators normally lack - it can make attendance itself the concession, and it must first solve the legal problem of landing a head of state under an ICC warrant, which is a bargaining chip disguised as logistics. The base rate is unkind to optimism: roughly 79 per cent of interstate wars end within two years, and this one is in its fifth, which is the region of the distribution where hazard rates fall rather than rise. Long wars get longer, and when they do stop the vehicle is almost always an armistice rather than a treaty - our ledger prices that at 85 per cent, on the Korea 1953 template.
brief.context: EPOCH: the post-1991 European security settlement and its collapse, whose ancestor rail is the 1975 Helsinki principle that borders change only by consent - the thing actually being renegotiated is whether that principle survives, which is why no text short of recognition satisfies Moscow. The desk that decides in Russia is not the foreign ministry but the Security Council and the president personally; Putnam's two-level game is the frame, because each leader is bargaining with the other AND with a domestic coalition that can punish a concession. MECHANISM: wars end when both sides' estimates of the future converge, and a battlefield reversal like Lyman pushes those estimates APART in the short run - the side losing ground has more reason to talk and less reason to concede. BASE RATE: COW data puts about 79 per cent of interstate wars inside two years, and long-duration cases show declining hazard; announced leader-level meetings that one side has not accepted convert to actual summits well under half the time. FALSIFIER: Peskov restating the 'deep pause, no new proposals' line after a formal invitation kills the move; a Kremlin confirmation of attendance, as an attendance decision rather than a peace decision, is what would extend it.

brief.head: Israel-Lebanon talks slip to October amid strikes in the south
brief.h: The US-mediated round scheduled for Rome this month has been pushed to October and downgraded to an ambassadors' meeting at the State Department, after President Aoun said in Nabatieh there would be no new negotiations while Israeli operations continue.
brief.t: Watch what an army does before a talk, not what a foreign ministry says about one. Israel detonated a reported 1,100 tonnes of explosives inside the Ali al-Taher ridge on 11 September and has shelled al-Mansouri, Douha, Arnoun and Wadi al-Salouqi since; at least twenty-nine people have been killed in two weeks. Thomas Schelling's distinction is the one that governs: an operation that CONSOLIDATES a declared line is coercive bargaining, an operation that extends past it is a campaign - and the framing both governments are still using is consolidation. What changed today is the political track rather than the military one. The June framework put Hezbollah disarmament into 'pilot zones', Hezbollah has neither disarmed nor agreed to talk directly, and the diplomacy that was capping this has slipped a month while the shelling has not - which is worth two points on our ledger and no more, because diplomacy receding is not the same thing as a campaign starting.

consp.claim: That the stated duration of every operation in this war was deliberate deception rather than planning failure - 4chan's long-running 'Persia Israel General' now headers each thread with a running counter: 'Day 1069 of the 2-Day Limited Military Offensive to End Hezbollah', 'Day 195 of the 4-Day Special Military Operation to Regime Change Iran', 'Day 22 of Operation Economic Outcome'.
consp.spread: The counter has run for more than two thousand thread editions on /pol/, with roughly 290 replies on the 12 September instance, and the format is copied on X and in defence-forum comment threads as shorthand.
consp.read: The joke is doing real analytical work and deserves to be taken seriously as data. A war sold as days that runs years is simultaneously a planning failure AND evidence about who actually holds the file, and both should be scored; the mocking version collapses them into deception alone, which is the part that is not established. The arithmetic itself is accurate and checkable. What it points at is exactly what our ledger prices - a campaign that keeps being framed as consolidation, held at 33 per cent of becoming an acknowledged multi-week one.

brief.context: EPOCH: the 1982-2000 Israeli security-zone model in its third revival, whose ancestor rail is the buffer-zone-plus-local-proxy arrangement that failed twice before for the same reason - a zone requires infantry to hold and generates the insurgency that justifies it. The desk that decides in Lebanon is not the presidency but the army command plus Hezbollah's own political bureau, since the state cannot disarm a party that outguns it; in Israel it is the security cabinet, where the coalition's survival is a live constraint. MECHANISM: Schelling's salami tactics - each slice is individually too small to justify a response, and the cumulative line moves without a single crossing anyone can point to. BASE RATE: of the postwar Israel-Hezbollah escalation episodes, most have terminated inside a fortnight under mediation; the ones that ran longer, 2006 and 2024, followed a mass-casualty trigger rather than a diplomatic postponement. INFLUENCE MAP: principal the Israeli security cabinet, agent Northern Command, narrator the consolidation framing, operator the engineering units and artillery, market Lebanese reconstruction finance, target Hezbollah's claim to be the only guarantor. FALSIFIER: the October Rome round actually convening, or a pilot-zone handover to the Lebanese army, would reverse the two points.

watch: An Aramco October loading programme for Yanbu, at normal volumes or not at all. With the ministry having confirmed the valve is shut, this is still the only document that separates a routing interruption from a production loss, and it outranks every statement either government makes.

Whether the Houthi HOCC's 'Safe Transit Request' stops being voluntary. That single change - a mandatory notice, or a charge for a named service - is what converts a captured island into a jurisdiction, and it is the whole of the new GEO-036.

Monday's meeting in Oman with Iraq and Gulf states on Hormuz shipping safety. Watch for a named administrator, a fee schedule or an escort arrangement: a toll regime always announces itself as a safety mechanism.

A Kremlin word on the Miami G20 - attendance, not a meeting. Zelenskyy's yes is the cheap half; the scoreable half is whether Moscow accepts, and whether Washington quietly solves the ICC-warrant problem that acceptance requires.

ISW or DeepState mapping that either confirms or fails to confirm the 200-square-kilometre figure at Lyman. Five points on GEO-014 are riding on a number currently sourced to OSINT analysts and Russian milbloggers rather than to a mapped front line.
lesson: Today's lesson is Glenn Snyder's alliance security dilemma, and it explains why a refused airstrike is a proliferation event. Snyder's insight, from 1984, is that every junior partner in an alliance fears two opposite things at once - ENTRAPMENT, being dragged into its patron's war, and ABANDONMENT, being left alone in its own - and that the two fears trade off, so everything a patron does to calm one inflames the other. The practical consequence is that clients learn far more from what a patron REFUSES than from what it promises, because refusals are paid for in credibility while promises are free. Scott Sagan's security model of proliferation attaches the consequence: states build nuclear weapons not when the threat rises but when the credibility of someone else's guarantee falls, which is why the historical cases cluster around abandonment moments rather than danger peaks - France and Britain after Suez in 1956, South Korea in the year the Nixon Doctrine withdrew a division. What that predicts right now is specific and checkable: Saudi Arabia asked Washington twice this week for strikes on the Houthis, was twice refused, and was handed intelligence and targeting data instead - precisely the substitution Sagan's model says a client notices and prices. The honest counter-case is that overt announcements are rare because hedging is normally covert, so the observable to watch is not a speech but an enrichment clause quietly dropped from a nuclear cooperation agreement, a reactor tender, or Pakistani personnel arriving under the Mecca pact - which is why our ledger's 21 per cent is deliberately a floor on a trend it cannot fully see.

Note that Russian milbloggers reported it first - a claim that costs its own side is worth more than one that flatters it.

quiz.q: A commentator writes: 'Iran closed the last route around Hormuz this week.' Which observable would most directly test that framing?
options: Whether Iranian officials praised the attacks
Whether Brent closed above $100
Whether the drones' launch province, operating group and airframe origin can each be separately identified
Whether the UN Security Council convened
quiz.why: The framing compresses three distinct actors - Iran, Iraqi militias in Maysan, and Ansar Allah in Yemen - into one hand. Baghdad's own investigation located the launch in Maysan and sacked the commander there. Who gains from the compression: the attributor, who gets to name a principal without striking anyone. Who pays: Iraq, which becomes a target set for someone else's war.

plumbing.epoch: E1, the 1973-79 rail on which oil was yoked to the dollar and Gulf surpluses were recycled into Treasuries, meeting E6, the 2019-21 plumbing-break-to-velocity-permit sequence still open in the form of an unended bill-buying programme. Today E1 was the one that moved, and a correction to yesterday's note belongs here: that security-for-barrels bargain is E1 in this module's numbering, not E4. Its unstated term was that the guarantor would keep the sea lanes open and would show up when a client was attacked. Both halves were tested inside thirty hours - the East-West pipeline shut, the Red Sea gate taken, and the guarantor declining a treaty partner's direct request for strikes twice while offering intelligence and targeting data instead. The old rail: a security guarantee underwritten by a navy with forward basing. The new permit: the guarantee is now explicitly partial - freedom of navigation for the lane, the land war behind it is the partner's problem - and the repricing that follows is denominated in hedging instruments rather than in barrels. DESIGN READ, gated and declined: no rail predates this. The refusal reads as drift and force-structure reality rather than as a plan to push Riyadh toward a hedge, and the incompetence alternative is straightforward - an administration that has said it will not start new wars discovering that its clients read that sentence as being about them.

sections.t: US diesel set an all-time record this week at $5.820 a gallon, and the crack spread — the refiner's fee for turning crude into something an engine can burn — printed an all-time $108 a barrel while Brent sat at an unremarkable $96. In the same week US missiles reportedly struck a tanker at Iran's Kharg Island anchorage, and Ukrainian drones held Russian refinery runs at 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since May 2002.

Crude — the thing everyone photographs and embargoes — is behaving; refined product is not. A $108 crack means the market will pay more to convert a barrel than the barrel is worth: a fact about cokers and hydrotreaters, not about oil. Name the mechanism — the conversion bottleneck. The binding constraint is never the abundant input but the narrow step in the middle, which cannot be built on the timescale of a war or an election.

sections.h: Deep history I — Rockefeller never wanted the oil
sections.t: John D. Rockefeller owned almost no wells. He owned the refineries of Cleveland, and what he did with them in 1871 is the founding text of chokepoint economics. Tom Scott of the Pennsylvania Railroad chartered the South Improvement Company, and Rockefeller's terms inside it were breathtaking: the Erie, New York Central and Pennsylvania would pay the SIC a rebate of $1.06 on every barrel it shipped — and a drawback of $1.06 on every barrel shipped by refiners outside the club. He was paid when his rivals did business. The charter was repealed that April before a single transaction cleared, and Ida Tarbell's exposé later finished the job — but the insight outlived the scandal: crude is worthless until someone converts and moves it, and whoever owns the narrow step prices the wide one.

sections.h: Deep history II — the war decided at the still
sections.t: The largest test of this proposition was the Allied air war, fought inside the alliance before it was fought over Germany. Arthur Harris of RAF Bomber Command believed in punishment: burn the cities, break the will. Carl Spaatz and Arthur Tedder pushed what Harris dismissed as panacea targets — oil. Germany had almost no crude. It had Bergius hydrogenation, synthetic fuel pressed from coal at Leuna, Pölitz and Brüx, plants too enormous to hide. The oil plan began in May 1944. Leuna alone absorbed 22 raids, 6,552 bomber sorties and 18,328 tons of bombs across a year, behind Europe's heaviest flak concentration. It worked anyway. German synthetic output fell from a peak of 316,000 tons a month to 107,000 in June 1944 and 17,000 by September. Aviation gasoline — the specific fraction, not oil in general — went from 175,000 tons in April to 5,000 in September: 97% gone in five months. From May 1944 Germany consumed more than it produced every month, and the stockpile was gone in six.

sections.h: Deep history II — the fuel, not the factories
sections.t: The detail that makes it unforgettable: over the same period Albert Speer drove German tank and aircraft PRODUCTION to its wartime peak. The Reich ended 1944 with more airframes than it could fly and more panzers than it could move — the factories were fine and the fuel was not. The US Strategic Bombing Survey — written by people with every reason to praise bombing in general — judged the oil and transport campaigns decisive and the city campaign not. Japan lost the same way: the July 1941 freeze is remembered as an oil embargo, but the fatal shortage was 100-octane aviation gasoline, a conversion capability Japan could not build.

sections.h: Deep history III — how the West stopped building stills
sections.t: Now the slow part. The last greenfield major refinery built in the United States was Marathon's Garyville, Louisiana: built 1973-76, online 1977, still running at 596,000 barrels a day. Fifty years, no new plants — and the base is now shrinking: about 132 operable refineries in January 2025 against more than 300 in 1981, with roughly 1.235m b/d of distillation capacity removed in seven recent closures and conversions, over 6.5% of the total. All of it while shale made America the largest crude producer in history at 13.86m b/d. The country built the well and stopped building the still. The capacity emigrated rather than vanished — Jamnagar runs 1.24m b/d, Dangote opened at 650,000 and plans 1.4m, China kept building — so the toll moved east and south, to jurisdictions happy to buy discounted sanctioned crude and sell the product back to the people imposing the sanctions.

sections.h: The pattern — and where it breaks
sections.t: In all three cases the scarce thing is the transformation, and transformation capacity is inelastic over any politically relevant horizon: a new crude supplier takes a fortnight, a new hydrocracker takes five years and a billion dollars. Ukraine is now running the 1944 oil plan at a ten-thousandth of the cost, a drone flying 1,550km to Omsk doing what 6,552 B-17 sorties did to Leuna — Pape's denial thesis tested live. It breaks against me here: Germany had no crude and no neutral supplier, Russia has both, and a 24-year low in refining has not stopped Pokrovsk.

sections.h: The adjudication — Yergin and Blas vs Chris Miller
sections.t: THE ADJUDICATION — YERGIN AND BLAS versus CHRIS MILLER Yergin and Blas hold that energy chokepoints self-heal — inventories, bypass and rerouting absorb shocks forecast to be fatal — and they have been right about the barrel, Brent at $96 in a war that curtailed over 11m b/d. Chris Miller's Chip War argues the opposite for inputs that are not fungible: no reserve of fabs, no bypass for EUV, a decade to rebuild. The evidence splits them by step. Yergin and Blas won the crude argument; the crack is the market announcing the win does not survive one step downstream, because there is no strategic reserve of cokers — the US holds hundreds of millions of barrels of crude in the SPR and about a million barrels of distillate in the Northeast reserve, having stockpiled the input it cannot burn. Miller's case is still weaker in oil than in silicon: diesel is shippable in a way a fab's output is not, so refining heals in 12-24 months rather than 12-24 days.

OECD gasoline demand is in structural decline as EVs scale; diesel and jet demand are not, because trucks, ships, aircraft, mining and data-centre backup have no substitute. But a refinery makes every cut at once, so the economics that close Western refineries — falling gasoline — destroy the distillate capacity nobody meant to lose. A trap, not a cycle; confidence high. The bolder call, near 60%: by the mid-2030s the US is at once the world's largest crude exporter and a chronic net importer of middle distillates, and that buys a strategic PRODUCT reserve — legislated storage of diesel and jet, enacted after a winter shortage rather than before one. What keeps this honest is GEO-026: does the US diesel crack settle below $45 before 15 December 2026? It sits at 35%, so the house is 65% on regime rather than outage — and if the crack mean-reverts on the 2022 schedule, this is an elegant story about a spike, published as a miss.
